ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is rectangle ABCD, the top side AD is labeled 6, and the left side AB is labeled 5; the right side DC of the rectangle is shared with the triangle on the right. A right angle is marked at point C, CE is the horizontal bottom side, and DE is the hypotenuse from D to E. Reasoning: The area of rectangle ABCD is 6×5=30. Because ABCD is a rectangle, DC=AB=5. The problem states that right triangle DCE has the same area as the rectangle, so the area of the triangle is also 30. Let CE=x, then (1/2)×DC×CE=(1/2)×5×x=30, solving gives x=12. Therefore the two right-angle sides of right triangle DCE are 5 and 12, and the hypotenuse DE=sqrt(5^2+12^2)=sqrt(25+144)=sqrt(169)=13.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram: rectangle ABCD has top side AD labeled 6 and left side AB labeled 5; since it is a rectangle, CD is also 5. The attached right triangle DCE has a right angle at C, with vertical leg DC and horizontal leg CE, and DE is the slanted side to find. From the text, the rectangle and triangle have equal areas. Compute rectangle area as 6×5=30. Set triangle area (1/2)(DC)(CE)=(1/2)(5)(CE)=30, giving CE=12. Then use the Pythagorean theorem in right triangle DCE: DE=sqrt(5^2+12^2)=13.
